newsitem.title: BELGIUM: City Bird aims for autumn take-off on Easdaq.
newsitem.headline: City Bird aims for autumn take-off on Easdaq.

text.p: Fledgling Belgian long-haul airline City Bird, majority owned by the City Hotels SA group, said on Wednesday it planned to list shares on the Easdaq growth stock market in the autumn.
City Bird would be listed at the end of September or the beginning of October, financial director Myriam Balken told Reuters. "Modalities will be set in the next few weeks."
The listing should help the development of City Bird and allow for the extension of its fleet.
City Hotels founded City Bird after selling its shares in EuroBelgian Airlines (EBA) to Richard Branson's Virgin group . No-frills airline EBA has since been renamed Virgin Express.
In June City Bird said it added a second MD-11 to its fleet.

City Bird operates services four-times-a-week to New York, twice-weekly to Los Angeles and once-a-week to San Francisco. It offers, via leading Belgian tour operator NUR, flights from Brussels to the Dominican Republic, Cuba, Mexico and Jamaica.
